item.title: Computing functions through the orbits of dynamical systems: the case of cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.34096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing a function traditionally involves constructing a formula, circuit, or program specifically designed for that function. But could a single, fixed computational structure generate an entire universe of functions simply by evolving over time? More generally, to what extent can the expressive power of a dynamical system be measured by the functions emerging along its orbits? We investigate this question in a setting where computation is driven by repeated application of one elementary operation, uniformly distributed in space and unchanged over time. Using cellular automata as a model of homogeneous dynamics, we consider systems whose states represent Boolean functions rather than Boolean values. Starting from a simple configuration containing only input variables and constants, the system evolves autonomously, generating new functions at different spatial positions and times. Unlike conventional function synthesis, no function-specific circuit, program, or operation sequence is constructed: the architecture remains fixed, and functions are identified by their space-time location. We ask which elementary rules can generate every Boolean function of a given number of variables along a single orbit, and whether this functional universality persists as the number of variables increases. We develop algebraic and dynamical criteria separating universal from non-universal behavior, and obtain a complete classification of elementary-rule symmetry classes for three-variable functions. Particularly intriguing is Rule 30, for which simple initial configurations generate all Boolean functions of up to five variables, suggesting possible universality for arbitrarily many variables. Our results support a view of computation in which functional diversity arises not from increasingly elaborate architectures, but from the space-time evolution of a single simple dynamical law.
item.dc:creator: Niccol\`o Castronuovo, Alberto Dennunzio, Luciano Margara

item.title: Locally eventually onto cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.33131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new checkable criterion to ensure that a one-dimensional cellular automaton on a finite alphabet is locally eventually onto. In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention. Building on Sutner's work with de Bruijn graphs, we describe a method for deciding openness and at the same time determining n. We then introduce the notion of block-regularity of local rules as a generalization of bipermutivity and prove that it implies openness. We further identify two conditions that, together with block-regularity, ensure that every nonempty cylinder set is mapped onto the whole configuration space after a finite number of iterations, and hence that the cellular automaton is locally eventually onto. The appendix provides the algorithms that check these finite criteria and then presents examples of locally eventually onto, non-bipermutive cellular automata for small diameters.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kristian Haugland, Nadia S. Larsen, Tron Omland, Henrikke G. Rustad
